look_here_first: First decide whether the plant is woody: black dalea is a low intricately branched shrub with many tiny leaflets on pale gray/straw branchlets and short terminal flower spikes.

project_inclusion.range_basis: 24-county boundary audit 2026-10-14: Hays, Kerr qualify; Val Verde out-of-zone and excluded from PASS. Previous evidence preserved in range_audit; third approved county pending.

best_field_traits: many tiny obovate to oblanceolate leaflets on odd-pinnate leaves
young twigs greenish to gray/straw and glandular
short terminal or leaf-opposed flower spikes
calyx nearly hairless outside but silky-ciliate around the mouth
morphology_keys.habit: Low woody shrub/subshrub, usually under about 1 m.
morphology_keys.leaf_morphology: Usually 4–9 pairs of tiny leaflets plus terminal leaflet; undersides gland-punctate.
morphology_keys.inflorescence: Short terminal or leaf-opposed spikes, subcapitate to moderately dense.
morphology_keys.calyx: Short-toothed, glossy/glabrous externally, silky-ciliate around the mouth.
morphology_keys.joey_field_observation: Joey Santore's Pilostyles thurberi study documents Dalea frutescens as the host and includes exact wild Sutton County host-shrub, stem, leaf and parasite-emergence images. Use these as trusted private-study habit/ecology material.

comparisons.key_distinctions: D. formosa has conspicuously plumose/feathery calyx lobes; D. aurea is herbaceous and densely silky; D. compacta is herbaceous with linear leaflets and a dense head.
